claims.text: An experimentally-induced increase in Facebook status updating activity reduces loneliness.
The decrease in loneliness from status updating is mediated by participants feeling more connected to their friends on a daily basis.
The effect of posting status updates on loneliness is independent of receiving direct social feedback from friends.

evidence.description: Results revealed that the experimentally-induced increase in status updating activity reduced loneliness.
Results revealed that the decrease in loneliness was due to participants feeling more connected to their friends on a daily basis.
Results revealed that the effect of posting on loneliness was independent of direct social feedback (i.e. responses) by friends.

methodologies.name: One-Week Facebook Status Updating Experiment
methodologies.description: A controlled experiment where participants were randomly assigned to post more status updates than usual or receive no instructions, with protocol compliance tracked via a lab Facebook Research Profile.
datasets: Facebook status update logs and responses
conditions: Experimental condition: instructed to post status updates more than usual for one week
Control condition: received no posting instructions

limitations.text: Prior research on the psychological consequences of online social networking lacks empirical evidence and causally-conclusive experimental design.
